amendment.reason: Full root-single GCC -Werror found default ConfigInit return could be ignored on an invalid stack-range path in both TCP and new TLS factory. Zero initialize the cold local and honor ConfigInit failure. Regenerate single; correct two historical README pending claims. All final functional/delivery/sanitizer/performance inputs rerun fresh; original cohort excluded from final counts.

implementation: 12 public xrpcTls APIs; same bounded duplex/frame/shared business executor and borrowed host Engine, only public native TLS/TCP APIs, no new runtime/thread.

Synchronous native policy/session snapshot, numeric client connect, deferred accepted-TCP handoff and one-time OPEN owned-TLS adoption outside callbacks; consumes exactly one native caller owner only on success.

Native TLS accepted-prefix offsets advance across header/body even on positive AGAIN; OK short prefixes self-wake; ERROR after prefix retains uncertainty, no replay. No full-frame adapter staging buffer; native record/ciphertext copies remain.

Original entry deadlines cover admission and TCP+TLS setup; bounded frame timeout, copied request context/name/ALPN metadata, per-turn bytes/frames/submitters and RPC ciphertext offer admission. Native control traffic separately bounded by Core Context/TCP, not MaxCipherBytes alone.
Typed terminal reason, copied negotiated version/cipher/resumed/opaque ALPN and error kind/code/domain; drain final buffered plaintext before EOF failure; protocol/resource/scheduler failures close.

Poll/Wait compose actual duplex/post/timer and public TLS/TCP retirement, release native owned data/session on Worker after native barrier, bounded cleanup backoff, exhausted timer quota needs Poll/Wait nudge. Engine remains pinned through Destroy; shared executor/Engine/external callers join separately.

xrpc_tls.description: Bidirectional native TLS and framing, independent of HTTP/WebSocket/DNS/process adapters

coverage: Two explicit framing formats, 1B/7B short writes and 3B/7B reads, bidirectional call/error/notification/batch, exact copied context/policy, zero deadline, cancellation after held business entry, four concurrent producers, retained result ownership.

Real buffered owned TLS adoption outside Open callback, callback-time adoption rejection, held native TLS alias blocks physical retirement, original native context drops exactly once, Engine pins/resources fully join.

Held verifier rejection before application writes, independent native raw TLS malformed headers/body limit/authenticated partial-frame EOF/frame timeout/final response+close_notify, actual incoming overload and held executor, constructor allocation budgets and actual timer quota exhaustion, stalled plain peer setup deadline.

Production-TU interposition over real encrypted sockets: 12 cases across both framings, short OK self-progress with incidental app Writable/Drain suppressed, positive AGAIN, zero refusal offset stability, partial MEMORY and unrelated Worker ambient error isolation. Private native struct access is test-only.

32 Python/OpenSSL TLS1.3 sessions per host: native client/server, two framings, 1B/coalesced writes and RSA/P256/P384/Ed25519 identities. Python client performs actual generated-CA PKIX+hostname validation; native client performs explicit DER+name pin, not PKIX. Validates bidirectional callback, batch/notify/null/Unicode/NUL/wide numeric IDs and payloads before closure. Ephemeral private keys removed and never archived.

Windows native regression; WSL ASan/UBSan/leak functional tests plus TSan single and production-TU probe. GCC unsupported standalone atomic_thread_fence instrumentation warning retained with -Wno-error=tsan. Generated features/amalgamation/API docs/maturity all pass.
cost_and_measurement_scope: Cold path: peer plus scratch/context allocation, native copied Session metadata and retained crypto policy, duplex/frame allocations, mutex/condition/post/timer, Engine pin, socket/TLS record buffers and cryptographic handshake. Ownership/context code stays borrowed through final destruction.

Steady path includes admission and JSON/result/frame copies/allocations, native record/encryption/ciphertext copies, per-offer public send-bound checks (bounded binary search under pressure), worker posts, timer deadlines, peer gate/counters and reference-drop mutex+broadcast. No end-to-end zero-copy/zero-overhead claim.

FixedBytes covers facade/scratch/copied request context only; FrameStorage/observed CipherBytes are separate. MaxObservedCipherBytes is sampled, not an instantaneous whole-connection peak. Allocator reservations, native pools/OS resources and other peers are outside facade figures.

Footprint single includes selected Core+RPC closure; static/shared primary size rows describe xrpc artifact only. Preserved footprint_artifacts include actual companion Core libraries with separate size metrics and forbidden-symbol audit; import archives are not runtime resident size.

Eight one-connection cases per host: plain TCP/TLS,7B/16KiB,window1/32; one warmup/seven rotated unpinned samples/eight separate heap runs,72 executions per host. Every echo byte is checked; CPU includes all process threads. Handshake excluded from steady samples.

Plain TCP has no TLS authentication/crypto, so rates are descriptive different-contract baselines, not regression or speedup proof. Throughput spread (max-min)/median <=15% is only a sampling-noise filter. Window1 closed-loop P50/P99 include caller collection and coordinated omission; window32 is a barrier window. No fixed-arrival P95/P999, connection scaling, pinned-host or production acceptance.

All own build/functional helpers completed before serial host measurement. Initial Windows process inventory still showed transient gcc PID23344 (no cc1); it was already absent at the immediate follow-up and no process identity could be recovered. Idle-machine isolation is not established; preserve runs without retries and make no performance acceptance claim.
failures_and_limits: All preflight failures retained, including initial compile/style/test selector/profile placement, premature accepted-stream TLS handoff and paused buffered ClientHello. Rejected candidate stalls after two accepted plaintext bytes when incidental write notifications are suppressed; archived candidate/log/executable excluded from final proof.

Standalone declaration helper initially retained a modular xrt/core.h include in historical certificate data fixture. Helper now copies equivalent public fixture bytes and standalone declarations with no modular include directories; no production workaround.

First full root-single WSL build reported maybe-uninitialized for unchecked default ConfigInit paths in both original TCP and new TLS. Cold locals now initialize and propagate failure; single regenerated and README historical status corrected. First Windows size run intentionally interrupted after root forms passed; taskkill returned partial failure while reporting unsupported already-changing descendants, and subsequent inventory confirmed all named processes gone before source changes. Full earlier cohort archived with hashes; all final tests/delivery/sanitizers/footprints/performance rerun on final source.

Native Linux servers, pinned Windows fixed-arrival tail/scale tests, full fault/OOM/session-resumption/key-update/trust-policy matrix, OS-handle baselines and all four-product >=72h acceptance remain open. Native TLS config/credentials/verification callbacks obey Core ownership, limits and nonblocking duties.

Framed DNS/prepared dial, stdio/WebSocket, transport negotiation, product credentials/recovery and other library release gates remain in the long-term goal. This stage does not complete xredis/xrpc/xmqtt/xcron.
